title: Late-ascent abort modes
body: If a single SSME fails between MET 2:30 and SECO, the abort mode shall be RTLS (Return To Launch Site) before MET 4:30, then TAL (Trans-Atlantic Landing) until single-engine-press-to-MECO capability is achieved. Crew briefed on which abort mode is active at each MET via voice loop.

title: Foam strike on TPS during ascent
body: Any foam strike on the orbiter wing leading edge or TPS tile observed via ascent imagery shall trigger on-orbit RPM (R-bar Pitch Maneuver) inspection at the ISS approach. EVA inspection authorised if RCC integrity in question. Direct entry NOT cleared until imagery clearance.
citation: STS-114 Return-to-Flight rules; CAIB Vol I (2003) recommendations

title: Protruding gap filler on TPS
body: If gap filler protrudes >5 mm from TPS line, ground analyses for entry-heating risk. If risk exceeds threshold, EVA removal authorised with a soft-handle pull tool (toothbrush taped to existing tool). Removal verified via post-removal RPM imagery before entry clearance.

title: Fuel cell coolant pump failure
body: If a fuel cell coolant pump fails, the cell shall be removed from the bus within 5 minutes to avoid stack overheat. Bus loaded onto remaining 2 cells. Mission rules require ≥2 cells operating for nominal end-of-mission; on 1 cell, immediate de-orbit prep.

title: RCS jet leak detection
body: Any RCS jet showing >0.1 lbf-s/s residual chamber pressure rise after commanded shutoff is flagged as leaking. Jet-isolation valve closed; affected manifold vented per MAL-RCS-3. Mission impact: ~10% RCS budget per leaking manifold.

title: EMU caution & warning during EVA
body: If EMU primary O2 pressure drops below 100 psia or scrubber CO2 partial pressure exceeds 7.6 mmHg, terminate EVA and ingress within 30 minutes. Crew shall ride backup O2 only as a last resort.
